changed.headline: Because of AI-read chest X-rays, Delhi's slum screening programme confirmed TB in 877 people among 168,568 residents screened.
Not because of AI: prioritising abnormal chest X-rays with AI did not speed up lung cancer diagnosis in five English hospitals, with median times of 44 days against 46 days.

Because of AI-drafted, dietitian-reviewed guidance, 66.7% of gastric and colorectal cancer surgery patients at one Wuhan hospital ate enough energy 30 days after discharge, against 40.0% given standard advice.
Because of AI review of routine chest X-rays, Goa's public hospitals have made 18 confirmed lung cancer diagnoses and cut the average time to diagnosis by more than 50%, the state says.
An LLM that drafted discharge documents for 153 children leaving a paediatric emergency department did not improve how well families understood them.

Because of a machine-learning model that found people overdue for bowel cancer screening, Geisinger patients who got nurse outreach were 6% more likely to have a colonoscopy within three months, and two-year mortality was 6.2% lower.

Because of AI-assisted chest X-rays, Malaysia's lung health pilot screened 14,350 people at seven clinics and found abnormal results in 25.5%, a third of them with lung nodules now being assessed for cancer and TB.
Because of AI, people in Tanzania with referable diabetic retinopathy were about twice as likely to reach the eye clinic within 8 weeks: 35.9% against 18.2% with standard screening.
Because of AI imaging support, stroke patients in western Sweden got to thrombectomy faster: the adjusted median from CT to groin puncture fell from 47 to 35 minutes, though outcomes did not differ.
Because of AI, Baptist Health in Arkansas says it has cut emergency-room boarding by about 525 patients a month, using predictive discharge analytics across its 12 hospitals.
An LLM screening 2,642 discharge summaries at a New Zealand district hospital flagged 102 confirmed cases of harm from care, and seven injury-compensation claims followed.

Because of AI, in-hospital deaths among high-risk ward patients fell from 23.1% to 18.6% after 11 hospitals let a deterioration model page the rapid response team automatically (adjusted odds ratio 0.82).

Because of AI, neurosurgery outpatients in Dresden who were given an AI-written plain-language summary of their own findings before the visit rated the conversation with their doctor higher, and the consultation was shorter (median 25 vs 33 minutes).
Because of AI, 52% of students with elevated depressive symptoms who used a generative-AI coaching app for six weeks improved meaningfully, against 32% given care as usual.

Because of AI, outpatient clinicians in a 14-hospital Boston health system who enrolled in the Heidi ambient scribe spent 1.21 minutes less on each note, though their after-hours note work did not change.
A machine-learning kidney-injury alert that sent pharmacists to advise physicians did not reduce major adverse kidney events across 38 hospital service clusters.

leads_added: Agentic AI for immune-related adverse-event review. [Nature Cancer](https://www.nature.com/articles/s43018-026-01264-6) (published 2026-10-29). Indexed paper sections report a randomized crossover study of 17 clinical research staff reviewing 20 notes each: AI assistance reduced annotation time by 2.71 minutes and improved accuracy and agreement. A separate silent prospective phase processed 884 notes during May–July 2025; it did not demonstrate improved patient care. Retain as a research lead: the current scout rules exclude reader studies without patients. A possible work-domain claim concerns faster, more accurate research annotation, subject to an explicit editorial decision on whether controlled annotation tasks qualify. Missing: full-text retrieval (the gate's reader returned `NOT READ`), verified dates for the randomized study, and source receipts before any entry is drafted. Do not use the publication date or the silent-phase dates as the achieved dates for the randomized benefit.
